subject: treehouse
pitch: A cozy treehouse diorama on a grassy round base. A thick old oak with a wide leafy crown, a little wooden cabin with a red shingle roof and a round window nestled in its branches, a rope ladder and a wooden swing hanging below, a pennant flag on the roof, a lantern by the door, and a few mushrooms and a bicycle at the foot of the tree.
reasoning:
I need a single efficient module for the diorama: a root joint at the origin since the builder requires one for parts, a base radius around 3m, a tree roughly 6m tall, and a cabin placed among the branches around y=3.2. I'm setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, spheres, and cones to construct the parts.

For the structure itself, I'm planning a soil-and-grass base, a tapered trunk with flared root cones, and a cantilevered deck platform jutting from the trunk to support a small cabin with a door facing outward, a round window, and a lantern by the entrance.

Adding shingle strip detail with alternating colors along the slope direction, plus the gable triangle fill using an extruded wood shape.

Still working out roof panel geometry...

Now I'm figuring out the pennant flag, shaping a thin triangle extruded along x so it flies outward in red and yellow, then planning a rope ladder hanging from the platform edge down to the ground using two thin cylinder ropes positioned on either side.

Then I'm using a helper rod function to build evenly spaced wooden rungs and tan rope segments for the ladder, and planning a swing hanging from a thick branch extending out from the trunk, with ropes running down to a seat.

Finalizing seat dimensions and rope positions, then planning the tree crown with clustered low-poly spheres at varying radii and heights, making sure the lower clumps clear the cabin roof.

Lowering the cabin to platform y=2.6 with height 1.3, adjusting the trunk to reach 5.6 with crown center at y=6.5, and sketching branch rods extending into the crown with a few highlight spheres for extra foliage detail.

Now I'm defining the platform deck geometry, support beams angled from trunk to platform front, railing posts and rails along the sides and front (leaving a gap for the ladder), and a taller lantern post at the left front corner.

I'm placing the lantern itself as a small glowing cylinder with a dark cone top, positioning the cabin's front wall with an arched door and knob, and adding a round window with a torus frame.

For the walls, I'll use a striped paint texture along the vertical axis to simulate wood planks, with dark corner posts for detail, skipping the chimney and side windows for simplicity. I'm also adding a few small mushrooms near the base with cream stalks and red, white-spotted hemisphere caps.

For the bicycle, I'm positioning it standing upright with a slight tilt near the front-right rather than leaning against the trunk, since that would be too complex to model convincingly, while mushrooms go front-left near the ladder.

Still writing bike geometry...

I'm also adding a small yellow basket on the handlebar, a kickstand so it stands upright, and scattering grass tufts, tiny flowers, and flattened stone details around the base for ground texture.

Now I'm defining a ground offset constant so trunk, platform, and other elements can all be positioned relative to it consistently, working out the exact heights for the soil layer, grass rim, and platform center.

Still placing coordinates...

Adding bark grain texture and a dark knot hole on the trunk, then positioning the swing branch with its tapered geometry and calculating where the rope should hang relative to the branch's curve.

For the ropes, I'm angling them inward so the pair converges toward the branch point, giving a natural A-shape to the swing. For the tree crown, I'm picking a mixed green palette and building faceted low-poly spheres in two rings at different heights and radii to create volume without perfect symmetry.

Now I'm adjusting the pole and pennant placement so it sits along the ridge near the front edge without clipping into the crown lumps—moving the pole's z-position forward and tweaking the overlapping sphere heights and radii to avoid visual collision.

Writing cabin walls and stripe coloring...

Now figuring out the roof shingle geometry with slope angle and panel positioning along the ridge.

Still placing shingle rows and ridge cap, then adding the gable triangle under the roof panels at the front wall.

Now I'm positioning the rope ladder and platform: a wooden platform box near the cabin's edge, with two vertical ropes running from the platform down to the ground, and interpolating rung positions along that slope.

I'm also laying out the railing system—corner posts and connecting rails along the platform edges, leaving a gap matching the ladder's width so it doesn't intersect the front railing.

For the lantern, I'm placing it on a wall bracket near the door rather than a post, calculating the door's edge position so the bracket sits just to its left, with a small horizontal arm extending from the wall to hang the lantern at platform-railing height.

I'm building the lantern itself with a small yellow cylinder body, a dark cone cap, bottom disc, and ring detail, deciding to skip a point light for simplicity. Then I'm positioning the door as a box next to the lantern, working out its width and placement relative to the window so the two openings sit comfortably on the front wall without overlapping.

Now I'm adding the door's arched top, frame, knob, and considering a step, then moving to the window: a disc for the glass, a torus frame, crossbars, and a little flower box with pink spheres underneath for charm. I'm also planning support rods running from the trunk to the front of the platform.

Then I'm positioning the swing, bike, and ladder so they don't overlap with the platform, setting wheel positions and sizes for the bike with dark tires and silver rims.

Working out the bike frame geometry, placing the rear hub, front hub, bottom bracket, seat, and head tube points relative to the ground height.

Adding a wicker basket box on the handlebar, a kickstand rod angled to the ground, and setting the frame rods to teal color. Then placing a few flat stones near the ladder using scaled icosahedrons.

Now I'm building a helper function to generate mushrooms with stalks and hemisphere caps, scattering a few near the ladder and one near the back, then computing spot positions on each cap using spherical coordinates.

For scenery I'm adding scattered grass cones with randomized radial placement and a few shades of green, then small flowers made from thin stems and tiny colored spheres positioned away from the mushrooms. I'll keep tree trunks and the cabin box using the same paint-friendly cylinder/box geometry, and decide to skip extras like a fence, birdhouse, or birds to keep things manageable.

Now I'm defining the root joint and part metadata, setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and rods with position and rotation, then writing the branch rods extending from the trunk into the crown using a bark color before building the crown loop code.
